name: Sahel insurgency
value: JNIM–IS Sahel rivalry; 64,000 fled to Niger
summary: JNIM and IS Sahel fight each other in Burkina Faso as both expand; UNHCR says 64,000 fled Nigeria to Niger in 2026
state: Al Jazeera reported on 13 Nov that clashes between JNIM and Islamic State Sahel in northern Burkina Faso have reportedly killed hundreds of fighters since September, including an unverified IS Sahel claim of over 400 JNIM deaths near Ganadaouri on 9 Oct, and that the rivalry has spread into Niger and Nigeria. UNHCR said on 10 Nov that about 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria to Niger this year (UN News). No fall or blockade of a capital or major city and no new mass-casualty spread to coastal states was found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Residents and travellers in Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and northern parts of coastal West African states face kidnapping and attack risks; follow FCDO travel advice. Arrivals into Niger strain scarce food and water.
rubric_hit: Watch: sustained insurgency; no capital or major city blockaded or fallen, no mass-casualty spread to coastal states
